Create a premium game-UI character ability sheet using the uploaded reference character, translated into a highly simplified geometric pictogram style.
LIKENESS INTEGRITY, HIGHEST PRIORITY

GEOMETRIC CHARACTER LANGUAGE

Use very few shapes per character.
Preserve recognizability through proportion, eyes, silhouette, color blocking, and defining traits rather than small details.
No realism. No 3D rendering. No texture. No painterly treatment.
GAME UI CONCEPT
Design the page like a premium character ability-selection interface from a stylish modern fighting game or action RPG.
Show 8 different ability icons or move states of the same character.
Possible actions: basic attack, defensive stance, dash, jump attack, charged attack, special ability, ultimate move, low-energy / recovery state.
Each pose must be dramatically different and instantly readable at small size.
No repeated pose logic.
ICON CARDS
Each ability appears inside its own UI card or tile.
Cards should use: rounded rectangular frames, restrained translucent panels, thin geometric borders, subtle layered depth, small accent bars, minimal corner details, circular or angular energy indicators.
The UI itself should feel sophisticated and restrained, not like a generic mobile-game menu.
CHARACTER ICON STYLE
The character inside each ability card is rendered as a flat geometric pictogram.
Use: solid color fills, simplified silhouette, very limited internal lines, sharp readable negative space, original character colors.
For action poses, subtle secondary graphic shapes may communicate movement: directional wedges, arcs, impact rings, speed lines, simplified energy geometry.
These elements must remain flat graphic symbols, not realistic VFX.
COLOR SYSTEM
Background: deep charcoal, graphite, muted navy, or near-black.
UI: slightly lighter translucent panels.
Character: original palette remains the strongest color information.
Ability accents: derive one or two complementary accent colors from the character’s existing palette.
Use saturation selectively. Avoid rainbow UI colors.
COMPOSITION
Wide horizontal game-interface composition.
Main character portrait or large neutral pictogram appears on one side.
The remaining space contains the ability tiles arranged in a clean asymmetric grid.
Allow different card sizes to create hierarchy: one large ultimate ability card, several medium ability cards, smaller passive or status cards.
Avoid perfect spreadsheet symmetry.
The layout should feel designed, modular, and playable.
TYPOGRAPHY
Minimal fictional UI labels are allowed only if necessary.
Prefer: tiny abstract symbols, short numerical indicators, simple level bars, iconography.
Avoid long text blocks.
If text appears, keep it subtle and secondary to the character imagery.
LIGHTING / VISUAL DEPTH
The character pictograms remain completely flat.
Create depth only through the interface: subtle panel transparency, faint inner shadows, restrained edge glow, soft background gradient, very gentle glass-like layering.
No realistic lighting on the character. No dramatic shadows inside pictograms.
UI DETAILS
Optional interface elements: health or energy meter, circular cooldown indicators, small passive ability slots, character-level indicator, selection highlight around one ability, subtle targeting brackets, tiny geometric status icons.
Everything should share one coherent visual system.
FINAL INTENT
The result should look like an official character ability screen from a premium stylized video game, built around a geometric pictogram translation of the exact uploaded character.
Clean enough to function as real UI. Graphic enough to feel iconic. Distinct enough that every ability is readable instantly.
No generic fantasy UI. No clutter. No photorealism. No 3D character rendering. No gradients inside the character. No excessive glow. No random interface text. No character redesign.
